newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada farmland value up 6.2 pct Jan-July 96 - FCC.
newsitem.headline: Canada farmland value up 6.2 pct Jan-July 96 - FCC.

text.p: Estimates of Canadian farmland values rose 6.2 percent between January and July 1996, a Farm Credit Corporation statement said Thursday.
The increase land value assessment was the seventh consecutive semi-annual rise in Canadian farmland values, said the FCC, a corporation of the federal government of Canada.
Quebec farmland values lead the nation with an increase of 11.2 percent in the Jan-July 1996 period, the FCC said.
New Brunswick values rose 10.5 percent, Manitoba was up 6.6 percent, Saskatchewan rose 6.3 percent, Alberta was up 5.8 percent, B.C. rose 5.0 percent, Ontario up 4.0 percent.
Nova Scotia values rose 2.3 percent while Prince Edward Island was unchanged and figures for Newfoundland were not available, the FCC said.
